Overall exposure risk is mitigated by risk capital requirements, as well as the SLL rate limits for deposits into the Spark High Yield USDS Vault (200M max / 100M slope, implying maximum of 250 million increase in total vault deposits within a 12 hour period) which would allow the freezer multisig permissioned on the ALM proxy to intervene if Spark planned an excessive increase in exposure to this pool. Parameter Summary: PT-USDe-27Nov2025 Pool supply cap: 1 billion USDS (increase for 500 million) [Ethereum] SparkLend - Increase LBTC Supply Cap Automator Parameters We have recently seen increasing usage of LBTC on SparkLend. We anticipate that this trend of increasing usage will continue, based on Lombard’s recent TGE, implementation of native yield for LBTC, and interest expressed by several large users. Lombard has demonstrated resilience and increasing lindiness over the past year, and liquidity for LBTC is adequate to support a higher level of exposure in SparkLend. Based on current onchain liquidity depth, swaps of up to 275 LBTC can be performed with minimal market impact, with liquidity dropping off sharply beyond this point. But we expect any further liquidations to be swiftly arbitraged against the primary market capability to redeem LBTC for native BTC. This is reflected by the resilience of the LBTC peg over time, where the largest downside price deviation of 2%, experienced on 6 April 2025 during a market drawdown, is well within SparkLend’s tolerance considering the liquidation penalty for LBTC in both normal and efficiency modes. In short, we find that LBTC has sufficient liquidity to support increased exposure limits, alongside sound fundamentals and tail risk profile. Parameter Summary LBTC Supply cap max: 10,000 LBTC (increase for 7,500 LBTC) Supply cap gap: 500 LBTC (increase for 250 LBTC) Supply cap ttl: 12 hours (no change) [Ethereum] SparkLend - Reduce Stablecoin Market Reserve Factors We propose reducing the reserve factors for USDC and USDT from the current level of 10% to 1%. This should make these markets more competitive and help with third party depositors and increase SparkLend market share. Spark has less than 10 million of third party deposits in these pools presently, so the benefit of growing the user base is expected to far exceed the lost revenue from reducing the reserve factor. Parameter Summary USDC Reserve factor: Reduce from 10% to 1% USDT Reserve factor: Reduce from 10% to 1% [Ethereum] SparkLend - Claim Reserves for USDS and DAI As part of Spark’s regular treasury and accounting operations, we propose to claim all accumulated USDS and DAI reserves from SparkLend on Ethereum and deposit them as USDS into the Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy. Parameter Summary: SparkLend DAI: Claim reserves and deposit to Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy SparkLend USDS: Claim reserves and deposit to Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy [Ethereum] Spark Savings - Launch Savings v2 Vaults for USDC, USDT, and ETH We propose to deploy and activate Spark Savings v2 infrastructure, beginning with vaults for USDC, USDT, and ETH on Ethereum Mainnet. Spark Savings v2 is an evolution of the previous v1 vault structure used in sUSDC. Instead of simply serving as a wrapper on the Sky Savings Rate as was the case in v1, Savings v2 plugs directly into the Spark Liquidity Layer as a generalized yield and liquidity backend, allowing Spark to offer vaults for additional assets like ETH and USDT that are not 1:1 exchangeable for USDS. This structure also future-proofs the USDC vault against potential changes in how the Sky ecosystem manages peg liquidity away from the existing paradigm of no-fee USDC swaps in the PSM. However, from launch we anticipate that the USDC vault will still allocate substantially all funds to the Sky Savings Rate as we view this as the best, most scalable low risk source of yield for USDC denominated assets in defi. Over time, we expect to roll out Spark Savings to cover additional assets and additional chains, positioning Spark as the core savings engine for the onchain economy. Additionally, Spark intends to launch a variety of value add services using Savings v2 as fundamental infrastructure. Parameters and details for the Spark Savings v2 launch are noted below. From an architectural point of view, the Spark Subdao Proxy (governance) is the admin of the contracts and controls upgrades, while the ALM Proxy is responsible for moving liquidity back and forth between the Savings vault contracts and Spark Liquidity Layer, and the Spark operations safe (2 of 3 multisig with hardware wallet signers) sets the yield of the products within governance defined bounds. In the near future, the rate setter role will be assigned to the ALM Proxy which will allow the rates of the products to be updated programmatically with the regular safeguards and fallbacks that apply to other ALM Proxy actions, but the relevant proxy version is still pending audit so the operations multisig will be used to manually adjust rates as needed until this upgrade is ready. We propose relatively loose max yields for each product, as we want to be reasonably sure that the max yield will not be exceeded in normal conditions (which would lead to outflows from users moving to higher yielding vaults from competitors), and the potential risk from the planner setting yield too high is manageable. The initial supply caps for each product will be set at roughly $50 million, to limit the maximum potential asset base while the products are still having their rates set manually outside of the regular ALM Proxy mechanism, and these can be relaxed once this is updated to permission the ALM Proxy with the setter role. Strategically, the products are planned to keep 10% of liquidity in reserve to service immediate withdrawals, with the remaining 90% deployed to generate yield. This strategy will be implemented programmatically via the ALM Planner software. This will allow ETH deposited into the Savings vault to earn a safe, low risk yield via the SparkLend ETH market, which is primarily collateralized by wstETH looping positions. This market has high liquidity and no unstaking period or queue, making it an ideal starting point for Spark’s ETH capital allocation strategy. Parameter Summary: Deposits maxAmount: 50,000 ETH slope: 10,000 ETH Withdrawals maxAmount: unlimited [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard B2C2 Penny for OTC Services B2C2 is a leading OTC desk for crypto assets. Spark Asset Foundation is planning to onboard with B2C2 to be able to take advantage of OTC trading services, which will benefit the Spark Liquidity Layer by enabling more efficient trading of stablecoins such as PYUSD and USDT. The initial version of the OTC integration is implemented as transferAsset rate limits of relevant stablecoins to the B2C2 deposit address of SAF. Maximum potential losses in the case of B2C2 insolvency or other problems is limited by the rate limits scaled by the expected time until discovery and resolution, so we propose to set very conservative rate limits initially to limit losses. In the future, this integration will be upgraded with a feature requiring the expected amount of swap proceeds to be returned by the OTC provider before releasing the next tranche of assets to be transferred out, which will significantly limit maximum loss exposure while enabling higher throughput. While the ALM Proxy is not currently set up to claim these rewards as part of regular planner operations, they can be claimed via a governance spell. Consolidating these funds will simplify accounting and allow funds to be reinvested via allocation system operations. Parameter Summary: Claim all aEthUSDS rewards earned by the ALM Proxy in the Aave Core market (roughly 243,167 aUSDS) [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Add transferAsset Rate Limit for SYRUP Spark is a major depositor in syrupUSDC by Maple Finance. This position earns SYRUP token rewards as part of Maple’s “drips” program, with the initial tranche of tokens expected to be disbursed in the near future. Adding a transfer rate limit to a liquidation multisig will give Spark flexibility to dispose of part of these tokens if necessary. Based on current market prices, the proposed rate limit would result in a maximum of ~$110,000 of losses if both the Spark Liquidity Layer and multisig were compromised simultaneously, assuming that Spark or Sky governance or contributors were able to react and freeze the SLL within 6 hours. Even assuming a longer resolution timeline requiring several days for a governance vote, the total amount lost would still be limited to well under $1 million, so there is no material risk to Sky or Spark from this transfer capability. Parameter Summary Recipient address: 0x92e4629a4510AF5819d7D1601464C233599fF5ec Transfer amount: 1,100,000 USDS [Ethereum] SPK Staking - Configure Symbiotic Instance SPK staking is built on top of the Sybiotic protocol for generalized restaking. This allows stSPK to serve not just as a governance token and recipient of Spark protocol rewards (such as Spark points), but also to secure critical infrastructure that Spark relies upon for its operations including oracles, bridges, and other dependencies. As of the present state, the Symbiotic instance for stSPK has not been activated, which means that stSPK holders do not yet earn Symbiotic points for participating in the network. We propose to activate and configure the stSPK Symbiotic instance to allow Spark stakers to earn Symbiotic points, while adopting a risk-minimized configuration to slowly ease into full restaking operations and ensure a smooth transition process. In addition to serving as the owner of the stSPK instance, Spark governance (via the subdao proxy) will also initially be set as the network and operator, ensuring that there is little to no risk of slashing events occurring. The maxNetworkLimit, which determines the maximum amount of tokens that can be staked to a network, is set as unlimited to allow all stSPK to begin earning Symbiotic points as soon as they are staked. Over time, we expect that Spark governance may decide to onboard additional operators and networks to enable stSPK to provide economic security to Spark infrastructure.
